newsitem.title: UK: Airfreight agents' association seeks new members.
newsitem.headline: Airfreight agents' association seeks new members.

text.p: The International Air Shipping Association (IASA), with 38 members in 35 countries, has embarked on an intensive global recruitment campaign, its chief executive Philip Turner told Reuters.
With a target of getting 50 to 60 members by 2000, Turner said this is focusing on the United States, India, China, Latin America and the Middle East.

Normally there is one IASA member in each country, although there are three in the U.S. -- respectively covering Baltmore/Maryland/Washington DC; New York; and California and the southern states excluding Florida.
Wherever possible they deal with each other on an exclusive basis in international airfreight trading matters, said Turner.
"We are now looking for four more U.S. members, to represent Florida, the rest of the west coast apart from California, the mid-west, and the central states from Kansas upwards," he said.
Likewise because of their sheer size, more than one member would be appointed in both India and China.
The association's member for India for the past 11 years, had recently resigned because it "failed to meet required IASA co-operation levels".
In its place, said Turner, IASA was looking to appoint new members to cover Delhi, Bombay, Calcutta and Madras/Bangalore.

The association had also recently received a resignation from its China member, China Resources Company unit Beijing Farenco Transportation, which Turner said could not obtain a required new 'A'-grade operating licence.
Three to four new members are now being sought in China.
"As for Latin America, we are a bit thin on the ground at present having lost members in Venezuela, Colombia and Argentina for different reasons," said Turner.
New members were being urgently sought in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina and Chile, to be followed by Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Panama.
In the Middle East, IASA has members in Dubai and Israel and is talking to possible new members in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman, Doha, Kuwait and Egypt.
The first of these, in Saudi Arabia, would be recruited by the time IASA's 52nd general assembly will be held, from April 27-May 1 in Manila, Turner said.
The 53rd assembly would be held in the first week of October at the Conrad International in Istanbul.
IASA recently moved its secretariat to London from Amsterdam, where it retains a sales, marketing and development office. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax +5017
